description: The name Team Triple A represents its three founding members: Abdullah, Abdul Basit, and Awais. The team is actively engaged in developing innovative solutions across the fields of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Computer Vision, working on multiple projects that explore emerging technologies and address real-world challenges. With a strong foundation in these domains, the members bring their technical skills, creativity, and problem-solving mindset to every initiative.
summary:
We developed the Pakistan Glacier Intelligence Explorer, an open, interactive web map that shows how Siachen Glacier in the Karakoram moves and how that motion changes. Using seven 12-day NASA–ISRO NISAR radar pairs (Nov 2025 to Aug 2026) and NASA ITS_LIVE annual velocity maps (2017 to 2022), our pipeline filters the data, calibrates it on stable rock, converts it to ice velocity, and tests change against measurement error.
This addresses “Dancing with the SARs” by using NISAR’s L-band radar as the primary dataset to track surface change through cloud and darkness. Our main results are that fast ice moves about 44% faster in summer than in winter, and that about 21% of the ice sped up significantly from 2017 to 2022. One tributary slowed by over 80%, which resembles the end of a surge.
It matters because Karakoram glaciers feed the Indus system but are remote and rarely monitored on the ground. Our map makes this data accessible to non-specialists, shows uncertainty for every number, and can be extended to other glaciers.
details:
The Pakistan Glacier Intelligence Explorer is an interactive web map of Siachen Glacier’s surface motion. We process seven 12-day NISAR L2 GOFF pairs (Nov 2025 to Aug 2026) from two tracks. We remove invalid pixels, low-SNR pixels, large offsets and outliers, subtract each pair’s stable-rock bias, and convert offsets to velocity. Where ascending and descending tracks overlap, we solve for flow direction. ITS_LIVE annual mosaics (2017 to 2022) give the history. Change counts as significant only if the trend is at least 2 standard errors and the 2017 to 2022 change is at least twice the combined error. Connected significant areas of 0.25 km² or more become hotspots. Users can switch layers, click for speed with its error, draw a speed profile along the glacier, and jump to hotspots from a table.

Results

  • Fast ice moves about 44% faster in summer than winter (63 to 94 m/yr).
  • About 21% of the ice sped up beyond measurement error from 2017 to 2022.
  • The largest hotspot is 17.6 km² on the upper trunk, where speed went from 117 to 173 m/yr.
  • NISAR flow direction agrees with ITS_LIVE within 7° (winter) and 10° (summer).

Benefits and impact
It gives non-specialists a no-GIS view of glacier motion, shows uncertainty for every number, and is reproducible, with notebooks, a test, download instructions and a methodology panel. It supports monitoring in a remote region that feeds the Indus system, and the pipeline can be reused for other glaciers.

Tools
Python 3.11, Jupyter notebooks, MapLibre GL JS 5.6 with a custom SVG chart library, and GitHub Pages. Check the library list in your requirements.txt before you submit, and add your hardware.

Creativity
It combines NISAR’s new radar with NASA’s long ITS_LIVE record, puts uncertainty first, and includes a test that recovers a known synthetic velocity field. The app works from 320 px phones to desktops.

Factors considered

  • NISAR and ITS_LIVE don’t overlap in time.
  • Summer radar has gaps from wet snow.
  • Vertical motion is too noisy (about ±18 m/yr) to report, so we don’t claim thinning.
  • NISAR products are early Beta/Provisional releases.
  • We don’t forecast river flow.
